historical.ss_analysis: Merrill argues that Steffel <ss> between vowels represents voiceless [s], not a Rarámuri geminate; his appendix explicitly gives nessé || nesé and nesséameke || neséameke.

modern_src02.provenance_warning: SRC-02 file identity unresolved and likely related to a pre-2016 Hilton lexicographic lineage.

independent_modern_phonological_mechanis.source: Caballero 2022, A grammar of Choguita Rarámuri
independent_modern_phonological_mechanis.process: optional /e/ raising to [i] in pretonic and posttonic positions
independent_modern_phonological_mechanis.relevance: The first vowel of historical nesé and modern Nisé is pretonic, so historical-modern e~i is phonologically plausible in a Rarámuri stress environment independently documented in a modern variety.
independent_modern_phonological_mechanis.limit: This synchronic Choguita process is not itself a demonstrated diachronic sound law linking Steffel's variety to Nisé.

independent_modern_lexical_support.source: SEP 2010 Awilichi bawi / El origen del agua
independent_modern_lexical_support.role: independent community usage confirming the modern shepherd-domain form outside the unresolved SRC-02/Hilton lineage

formal_assessment.reason: The apparent ss~s mismatch disappears under Merrill's phonetic interpretation, leaving principally a pretonic e~i difference for which Caballero documents an independent synchronic Rarámuri mechanism.

what_is_not_claimed: No historical sound law e > i is declared from this single pair.
Caballero's Choguita vowel raising is not assumed to have operated identically in Steffel's historical variety or Balleza.
The SEP community text is not treated as a morphological analysis of nise’ami.
Full cognacy and historical continuity remain to be tested against broader correspondence sets.
next_tests: Assemble multiple historical-modern Rarámuri pairs with final stress and pretonic e~i to test whether the pattern recurs independently.
Map geographic varieties for nise/niseami and related caretaker/shepherd forms.
Check whether historical/intermediate descriptions attest nise-like variants directly.
